title: Terraform module for IAM/RBAC scaffolding and least-privilege policies (private VPC)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module that scaffolds IAM/RBAC primitives required for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments and encodes least-privilege patterns for operators, control plane agents, and customer-admin roles. This module should be cloud-agnostic in its interface (inputs/outputs) and provide opinionated implementations for AWS initially (IAM roles, policies, instance profile, STS assume-role), with clear extension points for GCP and Azure. The goal is to reduce onboarding time for new private deployments, enforce consistent security posture, and make upgrades/rollbacks of role policies auditable and testable.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module publishes a versioned registry-style layout with input variables for environment, org, and control-plane instance IDs
AWS implementation creates least-privilege IAM role for control-plane agent with scoped inline policy and documented managed policy alternatives
Module outputs role_arn, role_name, policy_document, and a JSON artifact that can be consumed by control-plane for bootstrapping
Unit tests (terratest) validate generated policy JSON contains only required actions and denies wildcard S3:*, ec2:*, iam:* where not necessary
Upgrade path documented: policy migration strategy using incremental policy resources + canary rollout via feature flag in console
Security review completed and signed off by Security team before merge
technical_notes: Design: keep top-level module thin (inputs/outputs) and split provider-specific implementations under modules/aws, modules/gcp, modules/azure
Policy scoping: prefer Allow with explicit actions & resources over Deny; include explicit Deny for identity-based escalation patterns
Assume role trust: support OIDC or STS with external_id and condition on sourceVpc or sourceIp where supported
KMS integration: module accepts kms_key_arn and will generate policy statements granting encrypt/decrypt only for required resources
Workload identity: for future GCP/Azure support, expose variables to accept workload identity bindings rather than embedding provider-specific blocks
State: recommend separate state file per deployment and a naming convention to avoid accidental shared state across customers
Secrets: do NOT store long-lived credentials in state; module provides outputs for role_arn only and we store secrets in customer KMS/HSM integration in control plane
implementation_plan: Week 1: scaffold module layout, define variables & outputs, write README with usage examples
Week 2: implement AWS roles + scoped policies, add terratest assertions for policy JSON
Week 3: integrate with control-plane bootstrap flow (GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/4821), add example deployment for demo infra
Week 4: security review, docs, and automated policy drift monitor (policy-checker job)
Post-merge: backlog tasks to add GCP/Azure implementations and audit logging hooks
test_plan: Unit: terratest checks to parse generated policy JSON and assert allowed_actions == expected_actions per role
Integration: spin up ephemeral private VPC in staging and run full bootstrap using module outputs; validate end-to-end access from control-plane
Policy drift: create CI step that runs policy-lint and compares produced JSON against policy schema; fail build on new wildcard permissions
Chaos: simulate control-plane agent failing to assume role and validate error surfaces with clear remediation (missing trust policy or external_id misconfig)
rollout_plan: Publish module under registry path modules/iam-rbac with semver tags
Enable canary in one internal staging account and monitor assume-role success rate and permission errors for 48 hours
If no regression, roll forward to all staging deployments, then customer sandbox accounts, then GA for production private deployments
Provide one-click rollback by pinning previous module version in terraform lock file and running terraform apply with rollback var set
